reviews.author: YJ Oh
reviews.text: Located in Seongbuk-dong, it is Korea’s first private art museum. Although it may be relatively small in scale, it can be said to be one of the highest-class museums in Korea due to the value of its cultural properties. It was opened by Gansong Jeon Hyeong-pil in 1938 under the name of 'Bohwagak', and it houses and exhibits 12 national treasures and 32 treasures, including 'Hunminjeongeum Haeryebon' and 'Shin Yun-bok's Beauty in the Sky', as well as many other valuable cultural relics. We all know that 'Gansong Jeon Hyeong-pil', who was the richest man in the country at the time for generations, was a respectable person who spent almost all of his family's wealth to bring back cultural assets stolen by the Japanese and took the lead in protecting cultural assets from being exported to Japan. I bow my head at the thought that another type of independence movement was carried out to preserve the nation and its cultural heritage. In reality, it is more appropriate to view it as a museum, but this is the first time I learned that it is built on private land where descendants of Mr. Gansong actually live. Because the 'Treasure Treasures' exhibition was being held, I visited right at the opening time, but I was surprised to see many visitors coming early. Among the exhibits, the Goryeo celadon Yeonjeok, in which monkeys and hats sit hugging each other, is especially eye-catching. It is a wonderful place where you can appreciate wonderful works, and I hope that many people will be able to feel the greatness of Mr. Gansong once again.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Kal Korean Restaurant (Seongsu Kal) Gourmet Review
KAL Korean Restaurant in Seongsu is a place that gourmets spread word of mouth about. This small, unpretentious place serves dishes that immediately reveal their depth and honesty from the first bite.
The real attraction here is the broth. It is rich but not heavy, and the slowly boiled flavor combines to provide a traditional yet refreshing and clean taste. You can tell there was no rush. You can feel the milky softness and subtle complexity that comes from time, care, and sincerity.
The noodles were cooked really well. It's chewy and soft, and goes perfectly with the warm broth. It does not become soggy and retains its flavor well, showing the true craftsmanship of the kitchen. The side dishes are also full of sincerity. Crunchy kimchi, simple vegetables, nothing fancy, but you can tell it was made with care, with every ingredient seasoned to perfection.
The portions are generous and reasonably priced, and the atmosphere exudes an old-fashioned charm unique to the neighborhood. This is the kind of restaurant where the moment you see steam rising from a bowl of freshly boiled noodles, you already think of hearty soup.
Kal never follows trends. That's the strength of this place. Authentic, quiet and solely focused on taste. If you are looking for Korean food with a rich soup that you will remember for a long time, this is a place you will definitely want to visit again.

reviews.author: Kyurindate
reviews.text: I went to Seongsu Thai food restaurant Sonana Seongsu Station branch😍 It's a 5-minute walk from Exit 2 of Seongsu Station, near the Ark Valley Jisan Center, so it's easy to find, and thanks to the chang beer bottle and elephant props, the atmosphere is full of Thai local sensibility. Pad Thai Goong was made with plenty of chives, bean sprouts, peanut powder, and lemon juice, and the chewy rice noodles were soaked with sweet and sour and salty seasoning. It tasted just like the one I had in Thailand. It also had a generous amount of plump shrimp, so I was very satisfied. Tom Yum Khao Pad Goong is rich in shrimp and mushrooms, and the spicy tom yum flavor combines with the fluffy rice to create an addictive taste, but it is less sour, so it suits Korean tastes well. Men Bosha is filled with shrimp meat between crispy bread, so you can enjoy it neatly without feeling greasy when eaten with a lemon dressing salad. If you want to enjoy both the local Thai taste and atmosphere in Seongsu, I highly recommend this as a date course👍

I was really satisfied with the Tom Yum Spicy Shrimp Fried Rice because it didn't have a strong scent and the spicy and sour taste was perfect for the Korean palate. It also had 5 plump shrimp so the texture was great!!

reviews.author: cocooning H
reviews.text: I was looking for warm soup on a very cold day, so I stopped by Seongsu-dong's Pork Ball Soup Hau and was really satisfied. It's about 7 minutes from Seongsu Station, so it's easily accessible, and there's no big sign, so it has a quiet, hidden restaurant atmosphere. The soup of Hau Malgeunggongtang was so clear and deep that I felt my body melting from the first spoonful. The thin pork is topped with hijiki and chives, giving it a subtle scent, and the barley rice mixed in gives it a good texture. It was fun to eat it together with red pepper soybean paste, radish radish, and salted shrimp, and the meat itself was clean and without any unpleasant smell. The half plate of cold meat had a much richer flavor as the thick meat was served with water parsley and garlic, and the bitter and tangy texture of the dried herring roe went well with the meat. Lastly, it's perfect to soothe your mouth with orange! I highly recommend Seongsu to those who eat alone or are looking for a hearty meal.

After work in Seongsu-dong, I went to have dinner with my husband.
First of all, the food quality is crazy! The quality of the meat is really good and full of gravy. All of the side dishes were so delicious that I ate them several more times.

All the staff were friendly and the owner was so nice that I felt like I was treated well and had a meal. Parking is free in the basement, the building is clean, and the inside of the store is clean, so it's a place I want to go again.
